## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: how many games the 2026 World Chess Championship will last (as of 2026-10-01)

## 1. What decides the question, and where things stand
- **Current status:** the match has not started, so there is no score. The Wikipedia page for the match, last updated about 2026-09-29, also says it has not begun. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Chess_Championship_2026
- **Players and venue:** Gukesh Dommaraju (India, champion) vs Javokhir Sindarov (Uzbekistan, challenger). It will be played at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, Geneva. Both players will be 20.
- **Format, from FIDE's announcement:** "14 classical games. The first player to score 7½ points will win the match, with no further games played once that score has been reached." FIDE says a 7–7 tie is "decided through tiebreaks." https://www.fide.com/geneva-to-host-fide-world-championship-match-2026/
  - FIDE's page is dated 2026-07-28 by Wikipedia. One agent noted that Chess.com's announcement article is dated 2026-08-28, so the date of the announcement is **uncertain**.
  - **Range this implies:** at least 8 classical games and at most 14 classical games plus tiebreak games.
- **Tiebreak if 7–7.** All on one day, December 12. This sequence comes from Wikipedia and matches the 2024 regulations:
  1. 4 rapid games (15 min + 10 s).
  2. If still level, 2 rapid games (10 min + 5 s).
  3. If still level, 2 blitz games (3 min + 2 s).
  4. If still level, sudden-death blitz until someone wins.
  - The two rapid stages are confirmed by secondary press. The blitz and sudden-death stages are **not confirmed** in FIDE text; the agent did not read the official regulations PDF.
- **Possible tiebreak counts:** if tiebreak games count, a tie could end after 18 games (14 + 4), 20, 22, or more.
  - **Key ambiguity:** the question says "number of games which take place before a winner is decided." That most naturally includes the rapid and blitz tiebreak games, but the fine print does not say so.
- **Schedule:** the dates were revised.
  - **Original (FIDE release):** November 25 to December 15.
  - **Revised (WorldChess.com, 2026-08-29), "FIDE quietly changes dates":** November 22 to December 13. https://worldchess.com/news/fide-quietly-changes-dates-for-gukeshsindarov-world-championship
    - November 22: opening ceremony.
    - Games 1–3: November 24–26.
    - Rest days: November 27, December 1, December 5 and December 9.
    - Game 14: December 11.
    - Tiebreak: December 12.
    - https://worldchess.com/news/gukesh-vs-sindarov-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-2026-world-chess-championship
- **Other rules:** no draw offers before move 40.
- **Prize fund:** $2.5M in total, with $200k for each classical game won. If the match goes to tiebreaks, the winner gets $1.3M and the loser $1.2M.

## 2. Recent news and current form
- **Sindarov's results:**
  - Won the Candidates in Cyprus (2026-03-28 to 04-16) unbeaten with 10/14, a record score for this format, clinching it with a round to spare. https://www.chess.com/news/view/2026-fide-candidates-tournament-round-13
  - Also won the 2025 World Cup.
  - Named best top-board player at the Global Chess League, which ended around 2026-09-13. https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2026/09/14/sindarov-chess/
  - Samarkand Olympiad (ended around 2026-09-27/28): team gold with Uzbekistan and individual board-2 gold. His performance rating is given as 2797 or 2816, and his score as 6.5/10 or 7/10; which is right is **uncertain**. https://www.chess.com/news/view/uzbekistan-china-win-2026-samarkand-chess-olympiad
- **Gukesh's results:**
  - A weak 2025–26: last place at Norway Chess 2026 and 2/7 at the Chennai Grand Masters.
  - Dropped below 2700 on the live rating list on 2026-09-17, during the Olympiad.
  - Then won three straight games (2026-09-18 to 09-20), and lost in the final round to finish with individual silver on board 4. https://chessbase.in/news/team-india-secures-silver-at-the-46th-chess-olympiad
  - The Olympiad was reportedly his last event before the match (thebridge.in).
- **Ratings, September 2026 FIDE list:** Sindarov 2778 (world #4); Gukesh 2703 (#32, or #30 per Chessdom). The October list was not found.
- **Head-to-head in classical games:** Sindarov leads with 1 win and 2 draws (WorldChess).
- **Winner markets.** These show a clear favourite, which matters for length: lopsided matches have tended to end early.
  - **Polymarket**, seen 2026-10-01: Sindarov 73%, Gukesh 29%, volume about $95k. https://polymarket.com/event/2026-world-chess-championship-winner
  - **Kalshi:** Sindarov about 70%; date and volume unknown.
  - **Manifold**, seen 2026-10-01: Gukesh 31%, with 61 holders and 461 trades; this is play money.
  - **bet365**, 2026-09-02: Sindarov 4/11, Gukesh 2/1 (via OLBG).
- **No market on match length was found.**
- No news of any postponement was found as of 2026-10-01.

## 3. Base rates: modern title matches, 2006–2024 (11 matches)
These per-match figures come from the agent's memory and were **not checked line by line** against sources. They agree with well-known results.

| Match | Classical games scheduled | Games played | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2006 Kramnik–Topalov | 12 | 16 (12 + 4 rapid) | Tiebreak (rapid) |
| 2008 Anand–Kramnik | 12 | 11 | Ended early |
| 2010 Anand–Topalov | 12 | 12 | Decided in the last classical game |
| 2012 Anand–Gelfand | 12 | 16 (12 + 4 rapid) | Tiebreak (rapid) |
| 2013 Carlsen–Anand | 12 | 10 | Ended early |
| 2014 Carlsen–Anand | 12 | 11 | Ended early |
| 2016 Carlsen–Karjakin | 12 | 16 (12 + 4 rapid) | Tiebreak (rapid) |
| 2018 Carlsen–Caruana | 12 | 15 (12 + 3 rapid; all 12 classical drawn) | Tiebreak (rapid) |
| 2021 Carlsen–Nepomniachtchi | 14 | 11 | Ended early (7.5–3.5) |
| 2023 Ding–Nepomniachtchi | 14 | 18 (14 + 4 rapid) | Tiebreak (rapid) |
| 2024 Gukesh–Ding | 14 | 14 | Decided in game 14 (7.5–6.5) |

- **Ended before the scheduled classical games ran out:** 4 of 11. All four were lopsided, finishing 1–3 games early.
- **Decided in the final classical game:** 2 of 11.
- **Went to rapid tiebreaks:** 5 of 11, all settled within the first 3–4 rapid games. None needed blitz or sudden death.
- **Matches with 14 classical games (2021, 2023, 2024):** 11 games, 18 games (with tiebreaks), and 14 games.
- **Sources:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Chess_Championship and the per-year Wikipedia pages.

## Things to check
- Whether the question counts tiebreak games. The wording suggests it does.
- The final official tiebreak regulations for 2026.
- The October 2026 FIDE rating list.

criterios: This question will resolve as the number of games which take place before a winner is decided in the 2026 World Chess Championship.
razonamientos:
**(a) Time until the outcome is known.** The match runs from about November 24 to December 11, 2026, with a tiebreak day on December 12. The answer will be known in roughly 10 weeks.

**(b) Status quo.** The match has not started. The format is 14 classical games, and the first player to 7½ points wins. A 7–7 tie goes to rapid and then blitz tiebreaks. If tiebreak games count, which the wording suggests, any tie lands in the "15 or more" bucket. If they don't count, a tie falls into "14."

**(c) Base rates and model.**
- **History, 2006–2024 (11 matches):**
  - 4 ended early, 1–3 games before the end.
  - 2 were decided in the last classical game.
  - 5 went to rapid tiebreaks.
- **The three 14-game matches** lasted 11 games, 18 games (with tiebreaks) and 14 games.
- **This match looks lopsided.**
  - Sindarov is rated 2778 and Gukesh 2703, a gap of about 75 points.
  - Markets give Sindarov about 72%.
  - Gukesh's form is poor.
  - Lopsided matches (2013, 2014, 2021) tended to end early.
- **Simple per-game model:**
  - Assumed odds for each game: Sindarov wins about 25%, Gukesh wins about 13%, draw about 62%.
  - Over 14 games, that gives Sindarov an expected lead of about 1.7 points, with a standard deviation of about 2.3.
  - A tie happens about 13–18% of the time.
  - A finish exactly at game 14 happens about 18–20% of the time.
  - Most of the rest ends at games 11–13.

**(d) Unexpected scenario.** Gukesh is badly out of form and Sindarov wins 4 of the first 7 games. Sindarov then reaches 7½ by game 9 or 10. Alternatively, Gukesh recovers his 2024 form and the match is level at 7–7. It then goes through the rapid tiebreaks and possibly into blitz, which would push the count to 18–22 games.

Option_A: 3
Option_B: 6
Option_C: 10
Option_D: 14
Option_E: 15
Option_F: 14
Option_G: 20
Option_H: 18

(a) **Time left:** The match is scheduled to be decided between December 3 and December 12, roughly 63–72 days from October 1.

(b) **Status quo:** No games have been played. Fourteen classical games are scheduled, but the match ends early if a player reaches 7½ points. A 7–7 score would require tiebreak games, which I count because the question asks how many games take place *before a winner is decided*.

(c) **Base rates:** Of the last 11 championship matches, four ended before the scheduled classical games were complete, two were decided in the final classical game, and five required tiebreaks. Only three of those matches had a 14-game classical schedule, so these frequencies are a limited guide.

(d) **Unexpected outcome:** A run of decisive games—or a withdrawal—could produce a winner in 10 games or fewer despite the scheduled length.
